newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Megawati to defy office closure order.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Megawati to defy office closure order.

text.p: Supporters of Indonesia's ousted minority party leader, Megawati Sukarnoputri, said on Wednesday they would defy a local government order to close their new Jakarta headquarters.
East Jakarta Mayor Sudarsono sent a letter to the office on Monday ordering its closure within 72 hours on grounds that it broke zoning regulations in a residential area.

Megawati was ousted as leader of the minority Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) in June by a government-backed faction. Police subsequently evicted her backers from the official party headquarters on July 27, sparking the worst riots in Jakarta in more than 20 years.

Members of Megawati's faction, who opened a new office in the two-storey house last month, said after they met her at the building that they would hold a ceremonial meal there on Thursday, hours ahead of the deadline to close the office.
"There will be a ceremonial meal at one o'clock, and if the government wants to close the office...(they will come) around 5 or 6:30 p.m.," party official Kwik Kian Gie told Reuters.
When asked if Megawati's supporters would leave or surrender the office, Kwik said: "No."
Megawati's chief lawyer, R.O. Tambunan, also said her supporters would not leave the office.
"They will continue to stay there. We are not scared because we are not wrong," he told Reuters.
Tambunan said Megawati's lawyers planned on Thursday to sue the East Jakarta mayor over his closure order.
Tambunan also said he had sent a letter to Sudarsono on Tuesday, disputing the mayor's claim that the office was violating zoning regulations.

The letter, seen by Reuters on Wednesday, said local officials had given approval to the former tenants to use the building on a suburban street as an office. It also said there were already many buildings in the area that were being used for non-residential purposes.
"It gives the impression that the order for closure is not based upon legal reasons but political reasons," Tambunan wrote.
The military has said Megawati and her followers do not have the right to carry out political activities and that the opening of a headquarters was unacceptable.
The government has said it only recognises the rival PDI faction as the party's legitimate representative.
Megawati has launched a court case demanding that her ouster as PDI leader be declared illegal, and a further hearing is due on Thursday in a central Jakarta court.

The Christian-nationalist PDI, the Moslem-oriented United Development Party and the ruling Golkar are the only parties legally entitled to contest the general elections that are to be held in late May next year.
